addresses.name: CFixedWindow::DetachChildren
addresses.comment: CGuiObject slot 36 as CFixedWindow overrides it. Walks the window's two ordered child lists - the CGuiObject-relative +0x4C head (every child that is not a window) and then the +0x5C head (the child windows) - and for each node calls gui->vf[27](node->value) and then node->value's own slot 36, so the walk is recursive over the whole widget subtree. Node is 0x10 bytes, {CGuiObject* value; Node* prev; Node* next; bool}, and the next pointer is at +8. THE RECEIVER IS THE CGuiObject SUBOBJECT, i.e. complete CFixedWindow + 0x18, so every displacement in the body is 0x18 below the complete-object offsets this file records for CFixedWindow (+0x4C here is +0x64 there). CGui slot 27 is the shared ret-4 stub 0x60CD50 on CEU3Gui, so what the detach does on the CGui side cannot be read from this build. Named for what it does; the game's own name is not in the image.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole, 0xAC1220..0xAC1279, bare ret. vtable.py --holding puts it in exactly one RTTI table, CEU3DialogGui slot 36 (table 0x15CD494, object offset 24), and reading 0x1602058+36*4 and 0x15FFC68+36*4 directly shows CFixedWindow supplies this body where CIcon leaves the 0xABF890 stub, so the body is CFixedWindow's and not folded. [edi+0x28] is used as the CGui, which is a confirmed CGuiObject field, which is what fixes the receiver as the subobject. Four CFixedWindow bodies walk the same two heads the same way - slots 34 (0xAC4080), 35 (0xAC4140), 36 and 38 (0xAC4030) - and all four invoke CGuiObject virtual slots (17, 33, 36, 38) on node->value, which is what makes the element type CGuiObject* rather than anything else. Would be shown wrong by: a CGuiObject-table slot 36 on some third class that reads +0x4C as something other than a list head, or a node whose +8 is not a next pointer.

addresses.name: CFixedWindow::AttachChild
addresses.comment: CFixedWindow primary vftable slot 22 (table 0x1601F88; CEU3DialogGui slot 22 of 0x15CD3C4). Appends the name to the name vector at complete +0x30C, the child to the vector at complete +0x2FC (project.json's child_windows_begin), and then a freshly allocated 0x10-byte node {child, oldTail, 0, 0} to the ordered attached-children list whose head is complete +0x74, tail +0x78 and count +0x7C. Finally calls child->vf[38](byte[this+0x60]) and child->vf[25]([this+0x484]). The receiver here is the COMPLETE CFixedWindow, unlike the CGuiObject-table slots. Named AttachChild rather than AddChildWindow because FINDINGS-guilive.md section 5 measured the +0x2FC vector live and found 46 buttons, 20 child windows and 1 icon in it across 206 windows - every declared child window reaches it through this slot, but so does anything game code attaches, so the slot is not window-specific.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole, 0xAC2F90..0xAC3016, ret 8, so two stack dwords - which is what fixes the argument count. push 0x10 then operator new (0xB9602F) at 0xAC2FB7, the four node stores at 0xAC2FCA..0xAC2FD2, and the head-or-tail branch at 0xAC2FE5..0xAC2FEE. The complete-object offset +0x2FC is already project.json's child_windows_begin, which is what identifies the kind. Would be shown wrong by: the vector at +0x2FC turning out to hold something other than child windows.

struct_fields.name: child_elements_head
struct_fields.comment: Head of the ordered list of every child widget EXCEPT the ones attached through slot 22 (see +0x74) - in the order the .gui file declares them, across all kinds. Complete-object offset; the pointer CGui+0x5C hands you is complete+0x18, so this is +0x4C from it, which is how FINDINGS-guilive.md refers to it. Node is 0x10 bytes, {CGuiObject* value; Node* prev; Node* next; bool}. Filled by the CFixedWindow constructor's ordered resolve loop at 0xAC0DF0..0xAC10A3, which for each declared child name searches the window's fourteen per-kind containers in a fixed order and pushes whatever it finds here - unless the name resolves in the vector at +0x2FC, which goes to +0x74 instead.
struct_fields.evidence: Zeroed with its tail and count by the constructor at 0xABF94D..0xABF956 ({head, tail, count, flag} at 0x64/0x68/0x6C/0x70). The push is at 0xAC1060..0xAC10A0: tail from [ebx+0x68], operator new(0x10), node stores, count at [ebx+0x6C], and head written only when the count was zero. Read by four CFixedWindow virtuals (0xAC4080, 0xAC4140, 0xAC1220, 0xAC4030) at CGuiObject-relative +0x4C. A whole-.text scan from int3-delimited entries for a load/store pair through one base register at displacement 0x4C or 0x5C finds 38 sites and not one in 0xABF000..0xAC5000, which is why the writer had to be found at the complete-object offsets instead - the scan's positive control is that it does find the CGui constructor's own 0x4C store. Would be shown wrong by a push site that puts a child window here.

struct_fields.name: attached_children_head
struct_fields.comment: Head of the ordered list of the window's children attached through slot 22, same node shape as +0x64. Complete-object offset; +0x5C from the CGuiObject pointer CGui+0x5C hands you. Two independent writers: CFixedWindow::AddChildWindow (rva 0x6C2F90), which also pushes into the child-window vector at +0x2FC, and the constructor's resolve loop at 0xAC0F4A..0xAC0FBE, which reaches this list only on the branch that found the name in that same +0x2FC vector. NAMED FOR THE DISCRIMINATOR, NOT FOR 'window': the resolve loop reaches this list only on the branch that found the name in the vector at complete +0x2FC, and that vector is filled by nothing except slot 22 - the constructor has no build block for it at all, so a declared child window gets here because CGui's window factory calls the parent's slot 22. FINDINGS-guilive.md section 5 measured that vector live and found 46 buttons, 20 child windows and 1 icon, i.e. game code attaches non-windows through the same slot, which is why project.json's child_windows_begin on +0x2FC is a slight misnomer and why this list is not called child_windows either.
struct_fields.evidence: Zeroed with tail and count at 0xABF95A..0xABF963. The two push sites are 0xAC2FB7..0xAC2FEE and 0xAC0F7B..0xAC0FBE, identical code. +0x2FC is project.json's child_windows_begin, which is what names the kind. Would be shown wrong by a third writer putting a non-window here.

struct_fields.name: three_d_button_names

Nodes are the same 0x24-byte shape as +0x424's, with the next pointer at +0x20. The kind is 3dButtonType: the constructor iterates THIS list, calls the factory 0xAC6C80 for each name and inserts the result into the registry at +0x360. **Empty on all 206 live windows because neither the mod's nor the game's own interface/ folder uses the keyword at all** - 0 occurrences of 3dButtonType against 996/392 for positionType in the same grep.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xAC0A3D reads [ebx+0x434] as the head, 0xAC0A74 calls the factory, 0xAC0A83..0xAC0A94 inserts into the registry at +0x360 through its slot 6; 0xAC0A96 steps with [esi+0x20]. The same three-step shape appears for +0x424/+0x33C, +0x444/+0x384, +0x454/+0x3A8, +0x464/+0x3CC and +0x474/+0x3F0, which is what establishes the pairing index for index. The kind: the factory 0xAC6C80 calls 0xB30A10, which allocates 0x128 bytes and constructs the class with vftable 0x16094A8 through 0xACFA70 - the CButton-level constructor that writes 0x15FFA10 at +0 and 0x15FFB28 at +0x48, the same shape as CIcon's - and that constructor looks its graphic up in the objectTypes registry at CGraphics+0x6BCF0 (0xB5C41A: add eax, 0x6bcf0; call 0x9C7D60), which FINDINGS-gui.md establishes holds C3dObjectType subclasses. So the widget is a button whose graphic is a 3D object type. Second, independent discriminator, from CWindowType::LoadKey (rva 0x6C55E0): the type side has fourteen per-kind containers at a 0x10 stride from +0x174 to +0x244, and each LoadKey child case builds its child type with a distinct constructor - +0x1B4 with 0xB31940 (vftable 0x1606C40, textBoxType), +0x1C4 with 0xB2A820 (0x1606A38, instantTextBoxType), +0x1D4 with 0xB28120 (0x1606958, scrollbarType), +0x1E4 with 0xB29DC0 (0x16069E0, editBoxType), +0x1F4 with 0xAC81F0 (0x16021B0, iconType), +0x184/+0x194/+0x204 all with 0xB2DA90 (0x1606AD0, the type class guiButtonType and checkboxType share), and +0x1A4 with 0xB30490, which writes vftable 0x1606C04 - a gui type class FINDINGS-guilive.md section 3 never saw, because nothing declares one. 0xB30490 and the registry-1 widget builder 0xB30A10 are 0x580 apart, i.e. one translation unit, so the container at +0x1A4, the type class 0x1606C04, the widget class 0x16094A8 and registry 1 are one kind. That leaves multiSpriteButtonType for the container at +0x204, which shares guiButtonType's type class and whose widget (0x1609280, ctor 0xB5B310) is built by calling the ordinary guiButton widget constructor 0xB3FA50 first - a variant of a button rather than a new one. So 3dButtonType is the kind with its own type class that reads the 3D object registry, which is this one. Would be shown wrong by: multiSpriteButtonType turning out to be the one that reads the 3D object registry.

struct_fields.name: has_focus
struct_fields.comment: **Likely the keyboard-focus flag** - recorded as inferred because the merge takes only confirmed/inferred and the real strength is 'likely'. FINDINGS-guilive.md section 4 left this open: a byte with its own getter (CGuiObject vftable slot 2, 0xA800B0, mov al,[ecx+0x44]) and setter (slot 33, 0xA800A0), reading 0 on 2,304 of 2,305 live widgets - exactly one set. The static half: CFixedWindow slot 35 (0xAC4140) writes 0 here on itself and then calls slot 33 with 0 on every child in both ordered child lists, i.e. clear-the-whole-subtree; CFixedWindow slot 34 (0xAC4080) walks the child-window list comparing each child's name (its slot 17) against a string argument, calls slot 33 with 1 on the match, recurses with slot 34 otherwise, and returns a bool. Clear-all plus set-one-by-name over a widget tree is what focus is. Not visibility - that is +0x43, one byte away (trap 12).
struct_fields.evidence: 0xAC4147 mov byte [edi+0x44], 0 then the two child walks calling [vft+0x84] (slot 33) with 0; 0xAC4122..0xAC4131 calls slot 33 with 1 on the named match and 0xAC4100 recurses through [vft+0x88] (slot 34). Slot 2 and slot 33 read and write the same byte. What would show it wrong: a live session where two widgets have +0x44 set at once, or a keypress reaching a widget whose +0x44 is 0 - both are one-minute checks with a game running.

slots_noted: 0xAC1220 and 0xAC2F90 are recorded under CEU3DialogGui because CFixedWindow has no RTTI vftable of its own - the GUI framework was compiled without RTTI - so the export knows these tables only through the one derived class that does. The body belongs to CFixedWindow, which is why the names carry that class: reading 0x1602058+36*4 and 0x1601F88+22*4 out of the image gives the same two addresses, and CIcon leaves the corresponding CGuiObject slot as the 0xABF890 stub.
